senses.gloss: ch. same; also to set on fire.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 10:16">Targ. Is. X, 16</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 3:2">Targ. Y. Ex. III, 2</cite> <cite ref="J00567"><he>יָקִיד</he></cite> (Var. <cite ref="J00567"><he>יַקִּיד</he></cite>) being burnt into.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Exodus 3:3">Targ. Y. II ib. 3</cite>.—Y. Yeb. XV, 15ᵃ [read:] <he>ערקתא יקְדַּת וספסלה יקד</he> the strap is on fire (heated) and the bench is on fire.
<cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>לא ערקתא יקדת וכ׳</he> the strap was not heated &c.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:4:2">Cant. R. to III, 4</cite>, v. infra.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 5:21">Targ. II Sam. V, 21</cite> (h. text <he>וישאם</he>, v. <cite ref="J00560"><he>יְקוֹד</he></cite>); a. fr.—Pesik. Dibré, p. 112ᵇ <he>וא׳ היכלי</he> he set my Temple on fire. Lam. R. introd., end <he>סליק עפרא יקידא ואוקיד דרעיה</he> glowing dust came up and burnt his arm; Pesik. l. c. p. 114ᵃ; Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵇ <he>וא׳ זרעא</he> and burnt the seed.
Lam. R. to I, 13 קרתא יקידא אוֹקִידְתָּא thou hast set on fire a burning city (v. טְחַן); Cant. R. to III, 4 דרא יקידא יַקְּדַּת (Pa.), v. דָּרָא I.
